problems.description: Employees receive emails that appear to come from internal IT requesting credential updates. The messages contain malicious links that harvest login credentials when clicked.
risk_reduction: Enable multi‑factor authentication (MFA) for all user accounts
Deploy email filtering to flag or quarantine suspicious senders
Run regular security awareness training and phishing simulations

problems.description: The analyzed data represents a cybersecurity threat scenario involving phishing and spam emails designed to deceive recipients into engaging with malicious content. The malicious emails often use promotional language, urgent calls to action, and suspicious URLs to lure victims. Examples include fake job offers promising high income, fraudulent courier service advertisements, and classic advance-fee scams impersonating bank officials offering large sums of money. The emails mimic legitimate communication styles but contain embedded URLs and text patterns aimed at tricking users into clicking links or divulging sensitive information. The benign emails contrast with neutral, technical, or conversational content without suspicious elements.
problems.asset_targeted: End User Trust and Potentially Sensitive Information (e.g., credentials, financial information)

indicators_of_compromise: Email subjects with promotional or urgent language such as 'Part-Time opportunity - $2000/week'
Bodies containing suspicious URLs (e.g., http://www.largevalue.net, herrespect.com)
Use of urgent or enticing calls to action
Presence of classic phishing scam narratives (e.g., advance-fee scams involving large sums of money)
Subjects often include prefixes like 'Re:' or bracketed tags in benign emails but promotional language in malicious ones
Source categories correlate with label distribution, e.g., 'TREC-07' and 'Enron' sources appearing in malicious samples
attack_patterns: Use of multi-line email bodies with embedded URLs and disclaimers
Inclusion of special characters and encoded text to mimic legitimate email formatting
Malicious samples frequently contain repeated calls to action and suspicious URLs
Subjects often contain urgent promotional offers or suspicious financial opportunities
Malicious emails sometimes impersonate trusted entities or use social engineering narratives
normal_patterns: Subjects with neutral, technical, or conversational text
Bodies containing typical email formatting, disclaimers, and technical or academic content
Absence of suspicious URLs or promotional language
Presence of email/forum style subject lines with prefixes like 'Re:' or bracketed tags
Source values consistent with benign distribution (e.g., 'Ling', 'TREC-07' benign samples)

risk_reduction: Implement robust email filtering solutions that analyze subject and body text for promotional language and suspicious URLs
Deploy phishing detection systems that leverage pattern recognition of known scam narratives and URL reputations
Educate users on identifying phishing attempts, emphasizing caution with unsolicited offers and requests for sensitive information
problems.data_source_notes: The data preserves original schema and label distributions with realistic text patterns and source correlations. Malicious and benign samples exhibit distinct linguistic and structural characteristics consistent with known phishing and benign email content. Minimal null values and strict data type adherence ensure high data quality and reliability for analysis.

value_patterns: Short to medium length text strings
Often include prefixes like 'Re:', '[listname]', or other bracketed tags
May contain special characters, punctuation, and mixed case
Typical length ranges from a few words up to around 100 characters

constraints.format_pattern: Free text, often email or forum style subject lines with optional tags

subject.generation_instructions: Generate varied text strings resembling email or forum subjects, optionally including bracketed tags or 'Re:' prefixes. Maintain realistic length distribution and occasional nulls (~0.5%). Use vocabulary consistent with spam and benign email topics.
subject.relationship_to_label: Malicious subjects often contain promotional language, urgent calls to action, or suspicious offers; benign subjects tend to be more neutral, technical, or conversational.

value_patterns: Contains URLs, email headers, disclaimers, and natural language text
May include special characters, punctuation, and encoded characters
Typical length varies widely, from short notes to very long email bodies

constraints.format_pattern: Free text with possible embedded URLs, email metadata, and disclaimers

body.generation_instructions: Generate multi-line text simulating email or message bodies. Include realistic URLs, disclaimers, and typical email formatting. For malicious samples, include promotional or phishing style content; for benign, include conversational or technical content. Avoid nulls except very rare cases.
body.relationship_to_label: Malicious bodies often contain promotional language, repeated calls to action, or suspicious URLs; benign bodies contain normal email conversation or technical discussion.

label.generation_instructions: Assign label 1 for malicious samples and 0 for benign samples exactly as in original data.
label.relationship_to_label: Target variable indicating malicious (1) or benign (0) email.

source.generation_instructions: Generate categorical values from the original set of 5 unique source strings, preserving their relative frequencies if known. No nulls allowed.
source.relationship_to_label: Source may correlate with label distribution; some sources may have higher malicious rates.

value_generation_strategy.malicious_samples: Generate subject and body text with promotional, urgent, or suspicious content patterns; include URLs and calls to action. Use source values consistent with original malicious distribution.
value_generation_strategy.benign_samples: Generate subject and body text with neutral, conversational, or technical content; include typical email formatting and disclaimers. Use source values consistent with original benign distribution.

quality_checks: Verify column names and order exactly match ['subject', 'body', 'label', 'source']
Ensure data types match exactly: subject and body as object (string), label as int64 with values 0 or 1, source as object with allowed categorical values
Check label distribution matches original proportions (~51.3% malicious, ~48.7% benign)
Validate no unexpected nulls in label and source columns; subject nulls approx 0.57%, body nulls near zero
Confirm source column contains only the original 5 unique values
Perform text pattern validation to ensure subject and body resemble original style and length distributions
Check correlations between source and label are preserved statistically
Ensure no data leakage or schema drift occurs in synthetic data
